mentl/db3a0aa:
The graph encodes per-construction uniqueness via $lexpr_handle.
Emit was throwing it away, fabricating a single shared
`$variant_tmp` (and `$record_tmp`, `$tuple_tmp`) local across all
allocation sites. Nested ctor allocations trampled each other —
the OUTER's pointer lost when the INNER's alloc reassigned the
shared local. Demonstrated bug:

  fn sum(t) = match t {
    Leaf => 0,
    Branch(l, n, r) => sum(l) + n + sum(r)
  }
  fn main() = sum(Branch(Leaf, 5, Branch(Leaf, 7, Leaf)))

  Pre-substrate exit=7 (only innermost Branch's n surfaced).
  Post-substrate exit=12 (5 + 7).

ULTIMATE FIX, no band-aids: emit reads the graph. Per LMakeVariant
/ LMakeRecord / LMakeTuple, mint a unique WAT local name from the
LowExpr's graph handle:

  $variant_<H>   (was: shared $variant_tmp)
  $record_<H>    (was: shared $record_tmp)
  $tuple_<H>     (was: shared $tuple_tmp)

The graph already knew. The substrate-honest move is to read it.

two-top/dbbe450:
Four glyphs was never a name, it was an arcade constraint we inherited by
accident — the room code's CURSTAG wheel, reused because it was there. So
names are now up to 12 characters of A-Z and 0-9, typed on a keyboard with
a number row. 12 is not a guess: it is Xbox's gamertag ceiling and the top
of the 8-12 band that fits nearly every platform's limit, and it still
renders on a phone HUD without wrapping.

COLLISIONS, the way the field solved them. Riot's postmortem on unique
names is that hunting for an unclaimed one is where new players quit — five
minutes and a dozen attempts — so they split identity into a free-choice
name plus a tagline carrying the uniqueness. We need that split harder than
they do: with no server, nothing CAN enforce a unique name. But we get the
tag for free rather than asking for it, because the install-id is already
the durable identity — the tag is just a readable window onto it. And it
stays invisible until it earns its place: the ledger already keys on
install-id (two MORGANs were always two correct rows), so the tag appears
only once this ledger actually holds a second identity wearing the same
name. Meet one MORGAN, they are MORGAN forever; meet a second and both
become MORGAN#XYZ, exactly when the distinction starts to matter.

The wire keeps a fixed [u8; 12] padded with a sentinel: Copy, allocation-
free, and bounded BY CONSTRUCTION, so a hostile peer cannot hand us a 10 MB
name — there is nowhere to put one. profile.json stores text instead, so
the file stays greppable and hand-editable, and slots_from_name is total
(unknown characters drop, overlong cuts, lowercase folds).
